Organizational communication flows in multiple directions. Downward and upward communication are vertical forms of communication within a corporate hierarchy.

### **Organizational Hierarchy & Communication Flow:**

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Top Management / Board of Directors] -->|Downward: Policies, Orders, Instructions| B[Middle Management / Department Heads]
    B -->|Downward: Task Assignment, Feedback| C[Subordinates / Floor Workers]
    C -->|Upward: Reports, Grievances, Suggestions| B
    B -->|Upward: Performance Summaries| A
```

### **Explanation:**
- **Downward Communication:** Flows from superiors to subordinates (e.g., company policies, job instructions, notices). It is vital for maintaining authority and operational clarity.
- **Upward Communication:** Flows from subordinates to superiors (e.g., progress reports, feedback, grievances, suggestions). It empowers employees and keeps management informed about ground-level challenges.
proTip: Always include a simple diagram or flowchart when asked to illustrate hierarchical communication.
